definition: A neural network architecture with two or more identical subnetworks sharing weights, used to compare pairs of inputs.
details: Siamese networks are commonly used for similarity learning tasks such as face verification, signature matching, and few-shot learning.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Think of it this way: A neural network architecture with two or more identical subnetworks sharing weights, used to compare pairs of inputs. And here is the clever part: Siamese networks are commonly used for similarity learning tasks such as face verification, signature matching, and few-shot learning. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. And that shape of the machine — Siamese Network — is what makes everything else possible.
